scores.evidence: Phase 1 "Depends on: The Phase 0 skeleton"; Phase 4 "Depends on: Crash recovery (Phase 2)... and authorization (Phase 3)"
scores.rationale: Each phase names its dependencies and proves them with exit checks (fuzzer, chaos test) before building on them.

scores.evidence: A signed-in user opens `/d/:id` and types "hello"... second browser shows "hello". Reloading either tab still shows "hello", served from Postgres.
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is a real end-to-end slice deployed to prod via CI and Terraform, before any features.

scores.evidence: Flip to OT with a server-ordered log if (a) compliance requires the server to check and order every edit
scores.rationale: Many irreversible decisions are listed with explicit defaults and concrete flip conditions, including E2E encryption and schema.

scores.evidence: Tasks (widest → narrowest): Versioned document schema... Presence and awareness... ephemeral and never stored, so their blast radius is lowest.
scores.rationale: Every phase orders tasks widest to narrowest with concrete justification.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: OIDC login; TLS/WSS only; short-lived WebSocket token checked on connect; secrets in a secrets manager; no content in logs
scores.rationale: The cross-cutting table gives concrete security measures in every phase starting from Phase 0.

scores.evidence: OpenTelemetry traces cover `ws.message → apply → persist → ack → broadcast`... One dashboard. One page-level alert
scores.rationale: Observability is built in Phase 0 and has concrete metrics in every later phase.

scores.evidence: Terraform for all infra; lockfile pinned; image pinned by digest; DB migrations run in CI
scores.rationale: Reproducibility is covered concretely in every phase, including seeded fuzzers, golden fixtures and versioned load-test scripts.

scores.evidence: Load balancer health checks; client auto-reconnect with jittered backoff; daily backups with point-in-time recovery enabled
scores.rationale: Each phase has concrete failure handling, from Phase 0 through feature kill switches in Phase 5.

scores.evidence: N/A. The system has no AI or agentic parts.
scores.rationale: The plan explicitly declares the AI layer N/A and adds no AI components.

scores.evidence: Redis cross-node fan-out for hot documents. Pull forward when one document has more than ~200 simultaneous editors or saturates a node's CPU.
scores.rationale: The plan lists many deferred items, each with a concrete pull-forward condition.

note: Very strong plan: a real prod skeleton, dependency-proven phases, concrete flip and pull-forward triggers, and per-phase cross-cutting treatment. I found no clear weaknesses.
